decision: Treat hand authoring, back, and the graph's empty nodes and dead double-click as one change
why: The human meets all four while reading a tour and adding steps, and a fix to one leaves the others in the way

decision: A centre-tab switch is its own place, and each arrow-key walk is its own place. Scroll stays out of the comparison
why: Back was landing on the start of a collapsed walk, or on the tab the place was left with, which was correct under the old rule and not where the reader had been
result: unit tests assert one step per walk and per tab

decision: Do not record graph reveals as history, and do not add edit undo
why: A reveal is the same place with more nodes drawn. Edit undo is already deferred in TODO.md until a mis-click deletes work

decision: One add-focused control on the target strip, also on the Tours list and the Graph tab, plus the palette entry add step. It uses the existing add_step path
why: The strip is the place that already says which tour and step an add lands under. A second add path would violate the one-way rule

decision: callees_of returns the symbol's own callees. An empty list says calls not in this repo when the symbol still names calls or targets, and calls nothing only when it names none. No callers says no callers in this repo
why: The old list was the names inside the step's lines, so a slice step said it called nothing, and an unresolved call looked the same
result: unit tests cover both empty wordings

decision: Double-click on a node header brings References, and a jump that starts on the Graph tab does too. A definition path that is the real path of a symlinked root stays inside the repo
why: A header click only selected, and a graph jump never left the graph, so the double-click did nothing while References was closed. relative() compared path strings, so a canonical server path looked outside
result: ShowReferences unit test and symlink unit test

decision: Notes that still described collapsed walks, tab switches that are not places, and calls nothing for every empty node were rewritten. feature-show-references is a flow with one root
why: The features test refuses a feature with no flow tour, and check refuses a stale step

decision: Replaced assert!(x.is_empty()) with assert_eq! or assert_ne! on the length, and listed unused_self for callees_of
why: Clippy 1.99 denies pedantic assert_is_empty, and the arch lint refuses an unlisted expect. Cache has no len, so that one compares to Cache::default()

decision: Broke the tab comparison, the walk push, the unresolved-call wording, show_references, the symlink fallback, and add_focused. Each matching test failed. Restored the lines. The gui and io-lsp tests then passed
why: A test that stays green when the behavior is removed does not pin it
result: tests failed while broken, then 9 gui and 1 io-lsp passed

decision: Renamed the strip control to add-offer, the offer type to AddOffer, the action to AddOffered, and the empty status to SelectSymbolOrLinesFirst. shows_references replaces opens_references. callees_of is an associated function, so the unused_self expect is gone. The old References id add-focus stays. ShowReferences stays its own action
why: add-focused sat one letter from add-focus. FocusedAdd::Lines is not a focus. The expect existed only because the method no longer used self. Merging ShowReferences into ShowView would hide the gesture
evidence: crates/gui/src/ids.rs:82; crates/gui/src/authoring.rs:34; crates/gui/src/graph/build.rs:166; xtask/src/arch.rs EXPECTS length 27

decision: Hung the new step under step 2 on purpose. adding_the_focused_symbol_hangs_it_under_the_target failed with parent cccccc instead of aaaaaa. Restored Hang::Target
why: The earlier assertion only checked the step count, so a root hang would have passed
evidence: cargo test -p gui --lib adding_the_focused_symbol_hangs_it_under_the_target exit 101, then the line restored

decision: Rewrote the feature-show-references note. It names the closed References panel, the header buttons that stay, and why single-click and a new button lose. No throwaway prototypes were built
why: The case review said the note described the mechanism and skipped the goal, the cost, and the alternatives. Single-click is already move-node, and another button is the hunt the user asked to remove
